result.title: From Relevance to Validity: Zero-Shot Tool Selection via Functional and Contextual Validation
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly face tasks from unseen domains and execution contexts, making zero-shot tool selection essential for identifying tools that can satisfy task requirements. Existing dominant methods mainly rely on relevance ranking, but semantic matching alone cannot ensure that a tool is functionally compatible or remains applicable in a new context. We preliminarily identify a \emph{transfer-validity gap}, where semantically relevant tools may still fail to satisfy functional or contextual requirements after transfer. To address this gap, we propose \methodname{}, a progressive validation framework that complements semantic relevance with endpoint-grounded functional compatibility and task-conditioned contextual evidence. Across cross-domain and cross-dataset transfer, \methodname{} consistently improves capability ranking, with larger gains under functional or contextual ambiguity. Ablation results further confirm the complementary contributions of functional and contextual validation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文面向 LLM agent 的零样本工具选择，指出仅靠语义相关性排序存在「迁移有效性缺口」，提出渐进式验证框架，用功能性兼容与上下文证据补充相关性，并在跨域、跨数据集迁移中改进能力排序。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相关性≠有效性」的诊断与渐进验证/证据筛选思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中语义相关但功能无用的视觉证据筛选与推理期验证机制；但该工作针对纯文本工具选择，与视觉推理的距离需进一步判断。
